origin: Root proposed the exact same-prime pole and Landau sign argument; /root/madness_prime_math checked and wrote the complete derivation, source scope, ordinary-prime distinction and optional physical background.

sections.title: 1. Exact actual sector and new signed conclusion
sections.proof:
Use the literal q at scale1/4096, kappa=(D^2-1/4)q, H=kappa*kappa,
B=1/2048, and J=H*H. Write K(z)=integral H(u)exp(-zu)du, so
K(0)=1/16, Jhat(z)=K(z)^2, Jhat(0)=1/256 and Jhat'(0)=0.
Let P=[Lambda;H], S=P*P=[Lambda*Lambda;J], with causal zero extensions.
Split the COMPLETE ordered prime-power convolution into
 D(t)=sum_p sum_(r>=2) (r-1)(log p)^2/p^(r/2) J(t-r log p),
 C(t)=sum_(p!=q) sum_(a,b>=1) log p log q/(p^(a/2)q^(b/2))
                                      J(t-a log p-b log q).
Then S=D+C exactly. C is the coprime, DISTINCT-BASE PRIME-POWER sector;
it is not just the ordinary p*q sector. All powers, orders and source
factors remain. Every history on a compact time interval is finite.

The new unconditional DERIVED signed result is
 for every epsilon>0 and T, some t>max(T,0) satisfies
 C(t)<-(1/1024-epsilon)t.                              (1)
In particular liminf_(t->infinity) C(t)/t<=-1/1024.
Thus this genuine coprime sector cannot have an eventual sublinear
lower bound. This does not assert such a bound for the full S, nor
contradict a subexponential absolute bound: a linear negative term is
compatible with RH. No new Lean declaration is claimed.

sections.title: 2. Same-prime pole accounting with exact convergence domains
sections.proof:
Initially Re z>1/2, absolute convergence of the complete arithmetic
histories gives
 Shat(z)=K(z)^2 [zeta'(z+1/2)/zeta(z+1/2)]^2,
 Dhat(z)=Jhat(z) sum_p sum_(r>=2)(r-1)(log p)^2 p^(-r(z+1/2)). (2)
The second series actually converges for Re z>0. Separate r=2:
 sum_p(log p)^2 p^(-1-2z)
  =(zeta'/zeta)'(1+2z)
     -sum_p sum_(k>=2) k(log p)^2 p^(-k(1+2z)).        (3)
The subtracted series is holomorphic for Re z>-1/4. The r>=3
remainder in (2) is holomorphic for Re z>-1/6: on each smaller closed
half-plane, its geometric r sum is bounded by a constant times
sum_p(log p)^2 p^(-3(1/2+Re z)), an absolutely convergent integer majorant.
Thus both corrections are analytic near0, with no unpriced tail.

At s=1, zeta'/zeta(s)=-1/(s-1)+gamma+O(s-1), so
 (zeta'/zeta)'(1+2z)=1/(4z^2)+analytic near0.
Evenness of J kills its linear Taylor coefficient. Consequently
 Dhat(z)=1/(1024 z^2)+analytic near0.                  (4)
There is NO simple pole in (4). The entire source multiplier has not
been replaced by its value away from the pole.

The full Shat in (2) is analytic at0 because zeta(1/2)!=0. It is
meromorphic on Re z>0 and analytic at every positive REAL point:
zeta has no real zero on (0,1), has no zero for real s>1, and its pole
at s=1 is canceled by K's double half-zero before squaring. Therefore
 Chat(z)=Shat(z)-Dhat(z)=-1/(1024 z^2)+analytic near0,   (5)
and Chat is analytic at every positive real point. Off-real poles
from hypothetical off-line zeros are RETAINED; this is not a claim
of holomorphy on the whole right half-plane.

sections.title: 3. Actual positive-Laplace argument, including the finite prefix
sections.proof:
Put c0=1/1024. Suppose (1) fails for some 0<epsilon<c0 and some
T>=0. Then C(t)+(c0-epsilon)t>=0 for every t>=T. Set
 u(t)=1_[T,infinity)(t)[C(t)+(c0-epsilon)t].
This is a measurable, nonnegative actual function. Compact-source
Chebyshev bounds give |S(t)|<=C(1+t)exp(t/2). For D, an active p^r
has r<=O(1+t), p<=exp((t+2B)/r) and p^(-r/2)<=exp(-(t-2B)/2).
Counting by ALL integers gives the r=2 part O((1+t)^2) and the
r>=3 total O((1+t)^4 exp(-t/6)). Thus u has a nonempty genuine
Laplace-integrability domain containing every real sigma>1/2.
In that safe half-plane its transform is
 Uhat(z)=Chat(z)+(c0-epsilon)/z^2-E_T(z),
 E_T(z)=integral_0^T exp(-zt)[C(t)+(c0-epsilon)t]dt.    (6)
E_T is ENTIRE, because the prefix is finite and locally smooth. It is
not an omitted boundary term. Equations (5)-(6) give the meromorphic
continuation Uhat(z)=-epsilon/z^2+analytic near0.

Positivity makes the actual integrability domain upward closed. If
it is unbounded below, it already contains every positive parameter.
Otherwise let sigma_c be its finite infimum. If sigma_c>0, the
current PositiveLaplaceBoundary theorem forbids an analytic continuation
at this actual real abscissa. But (6) is analytic there by section2.
Agreement on the right part of a small disk follows from the initial
safe identity and meromorphic identity continuation on the connected
half-plane Re z>sigma_c, exactly as in UniversalSincSignedExcursions.
The positive transform is holomorphic there; any off-real singularities
of (6) in that domain must therefore be removable under this hypothesis.
This local agreement is not assumed and does not erase off-line poles
unconditionally. It gives the Landau contradiction if sigma_c>0.

Hence in either domain case the actual nonnegative transform converges
and agrees with (6) for every real sigma>0. Let sigma decrease to0:
 integral_T^infinity exp(-sigma*t)u(t)dt
       =-epsilon/sigma^2+O(1)<0 for small sigma>0,
which is impossible. This proves (1). No integral at sigma=0, critical-
line Fourier substitution, assumed RH, rightmost zero, or endpoint
convergence is used. Epsilon>=c0 cases follow from a smaller positive
epsilon, so the displayed quantifier in (1) is valid.

sections.title: 4. What the same-prime background means in physical time
sections.proof:
The signed conclusion above does NOT need PNT. An additional optional
physical interpretation follows from the already used quantitative PNT
theta_p(x)=sum_(p<=x)log p=x+O(x exp(-c sqrt(log x))).
For the r=2 term, Stieltjes summation of
 integral (log x)/x J(t-2log x) dtheta_p(x)
gives the exact main
 (1/4)integral (t-u)J(u)du=t/1024.
The derivative of (log x)/x and of J are both retained; the compact
support gives error O((1+t)exp(-c1 sqrt(t))). Its endpoints vanish.
The r>=3 terms are O((1+t)^A exp(-t/6)) for some fixed A, by summing
the elementary prime/integer majorants over r<=O(t), including the
bounded number of small primes. Consequently D(t)=t/1024+o(1).

This is a price for the separate same-prime background, not a bound
on C or S. The negative excursions in (1) show that the full coprime
sector compensates that background cofinally. They do not say the
compensation is pointwise exact or that C(t)/t converges.
Primary paper input for this optional paragraph only: Elkies, Math229
PNT proof, theorem(1), pages1-2, https://people.math.harvard.edu/~elkies/M229.09/pnt.pdf,
opened directly for this pass. No downloaded-PDF byte hash or new
compiled PNT authority is claimed.

sections.title: 5. Ordinary-prime-only scope and canonical compensation
sections.proof:
The power distinction is essential. Let P1 use only ordinary primes
and Pge2=P-P1. Near z=0, its arithmetic transform satisfies
 Phat_ge2(z)=1/(32z)+analytic,
 because its r=2 term is K(z)[-zeta'/zeta(1+2z) minus the k>=2
 correction], and all r>=3 terms are analytic near0. K(0)=1/16,
so the pole coefficient is1/32. Thus
 Phat_1(z)=-1/(32z)+analytic.
The ordinary-prime self-echo has positive double coefficient1/1024;
its same-prime square diagonal has exactly the same coefficient.
They cancel on subtraction. Therefore the negative-double-pole proof
in sections2-3 DOES NOT establish (1) for ordinary-prime-only coprime
p*q pairs. No such promotion is made.

The canonical complete echo remains
 E_W(L)=S(L-2c)+2(P_c*a_c)(L)+(a_c*a_c)(L).
It includes the SAME D+C, with all Arch and causal-prefix terms retained.
Likewise the full Mobius hyperbola identity P=2E-T and its rank-one
compensation remain unchanged. Formula (1) supplies an actual signed
restriction on one exact arithmetic sector, not a lower/upper bound
on the fully compensated total. It falsifies eventual nonnegativity
and every sublinear lower bound for C alone; it does not prove the
target-specific subexponential estimate or RH.

This differs from the earlier pointwise-square Landau report: that
report's transform was a vertical convolution with possible real-axis
pinches. Here S is TIME self-convolution, its transform is Phat^2,
and subtraction of the exact same-prime term creates the negative
real double pole (5). Confusing these two objects invalidates the proof.
